correctness.rationale: Exact reconstruction from a regular dodecagon yields exactly 49 lines and reproduces the published singularity census. The unique 12-fold point must be fixed and the 12 sevenfold points permuted by every projective stabilizer. A projective frame consisting of that point and three sevenfold points reduces exhaustion to 1320 ordered image triples; exact frame reconstruction leaves exactly 24 stabilizers. The visible rotation and reflection generate a dihedral subgroup of order 24, so the full stabilizer is \(D_{12}\).

value.rationale: The source presents \(\mathcal O_{49}\) as a rigid free arrangement arising from a highly symmetric regular-polygon construction. Determining whether the evident dodecagonal symmetry is the whole projective symmetry group is a natural structural question: rigidity does not settle it, and extra projective symmetries can occur in special configurations. The result gives the exact group and its complete line-orbit structure, including the unique fixed line at infinity.
